grh_72d003aab209dbaf7085.title: The Terrifying Cats
paragraphs: In Rome, celebrated soprano Gina Valkazi secretly asks Holmes for help, then publicly denies sending for him. Soon the singer is found collapsed in a dressing room filled with cats and appears to have lost her voice, giving young understudy Lisa Bordoni a sudden triumph and making her a target for an angry crowd. Holmes learns Valkazi had an identical twin, Bella, who shared her appearance but not her voice. Bella had murdered the real singer, assumed her identity and staged the cat panic so the impostor's inability to sing would seem permanent. Holmes slips a cat into her room; her lack of fear proves the substitution, and he forces the impostor to confess from the balcony before the mob can attack Lisa.

This [[show|the-new-adventures-of-sherlock-holmes|The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes]] broadcast aired on February 25, 1946. [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Eric Snowdon. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Anthony Boucher as writer, Denis Green as writer, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.cf0fae063e7e9aa4|The Adventure of Black Peter]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_72de1c70bd89b3f4dcfb.title: Shadow of a Doubt
paragraphs: Young Charlie Newton is thrilled when her adored Uncle Charlie visits the family in Santa Rosa, but clues from two investigators and a newspaper story make her realize he is the wanted 'Merry Widow Murderer.' She keeps silent to protect her mother while trying to force him to leave, and Uncle Charlie responds by attempting to kill her, including trapping her in a garage filling with exhaust. Their final struggle ends with Uncle Charlie dead, while the family believes his death was accidental.
